sources.entry: Desktop Profiles - An innovative desktop/window manager for macOS

summary.one_liner: Desktop Profiles is a macOS utility for switching between user-defined workspace profiles that restore window layouts, app states, and system settings.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a tool for moving between work environments on macOS. Each user-defined profile stores a container for caching app internal states and a window arrangement. When a profile is invoked, the README says windows are rearranged and selected apps' internal states restored. Profiles can also set system settings such as theme, accent colour, and Night Shift. Other applications can be closed or left open, and assigned workflows are executed. Profiles can be invoked by a keyboard shortcut, according to the demo section. The README also mentions a remote-control proof of concept in the source code, which requires building the app yourself.
use_cases: switch between work and personal workspaces on mac
restore window layout for a task
change theme and accent colour per profile
open a set of apps at once
classroom remote workspace switching (proof of concept)
how_to_run: Download the prebuilt version from the link in the README
notable: Profiles restore both window arrangement and internal state of selected apps
Can set system theme, accent colour, and Night Shift per profile
Profiles can be invoked via keyboard shortcut
Originally developed for a Czech science fair (SOČ) project
caveats: Requires macOS; the README does not state supported macOS versions
Remote-control feature is only a proof of concept and requires building from source
The paper describing development is available only in Czech
